frame:
PLAYER EXPERIENCE FIRST — what the two PCs actually do at levels 1-5, before any spreadsheet.

LEVEL 1, THE WHITE PC. White has five depth-0 nodes (Terms of Accord, Guardian Stance, Guiding Signal, Pillar of Order, the free Key), but Pillar of Order is White 3+ = L6, so the player picks ONE of three. All three hand the effect to someone else: Guardian Stance is "+1 Deflect while an ally is adjacent" (a Passive), Terms of Accord is a Special that grants +1 to tests pursuing an agreed objective, and Guiding Signal is a 1-Action, 1-Investiture play whose entire output is that the NEXT ALLY who tests against the marked enemy raises the stakes. Zero of the three produce an effect the White player resolves themselves. A level-1 White turn is: Draw Mana (1 Action, +1 Investiture, allies in range regain 1 HP), Strike with a weapon no talent supports, Move. That is the session-one experience, and it is not "I do no damage" — it is "my sheet gives me nothing to spend an Action on."

LEVEL 1, THE BLUE PC. Blue also offers three real picks: Calculated Patience (Passive), Forewarned (Passive), Phantom Double. Phantom Double is Blue's only active level-1 talent and it is the most expensive depth-0 talent in the leyline atlas: 2 of 3 Actions and 2 of a ~4 Investiture pool, to create a 1-health decoy that any hit destroys. Blue's problem is the mirror of White's: Blue has things to DO and none of them produce anything the player or the table can point at.

THE CONTRAST THAT WILL BE FELT AT THE TABLE. A level-1 Black PC picks Withering Ray — 1 Action, no Investiture, 2d6 vital that ignores Deflect — or Hollow Command, 2 Actions, the enemy loses its entire next turn. A level-1 Red PC has three 1-Action plays. Green has Verdant Mend. Every colour offers exactly three level-1 picks; Red's are 3-for-3 self-resolving, Black's 2-for-3, Green's 1-for-3, Blue's 1-for-3 and overpriced, White's 0-for-3.

LEVELS 2-5. White accretes Reactions — Counterpoint, Interposing Shield, Retributive Guard, later Shared Burden and Voice of Authority — seven in total competing for one Reaction per round, three of which (Interposing Shield, Retributive Guard, Shared Burden) fire on the identical event "an ally near me took damage." Every one of them waits on another creature to be hurt first. The numbers are 1 HP of healing, +1 Deflect, and half [Die] = ~1.75 points of damage reduction. Blue accretes a wall, a 5 ft push, and four talents that impose disadvantage — which the primer settles is ONE binary scalar the engine boolean-ORs, so Blue's signature lever is the least additive effect in the game and Blue owns a third of the corpus's instances of it. Blue's three actual teeth — Counterspell, Ghostly Walls, Absolute Stillness — are all Blue 3+, i.e. level 6, half the campaign away.

THE "MY THING IS THE SAME AS THEIR THING" PROBLEM IS REAL BUT MIS-LOCATED. Function-vector cosine puts White<->Blue at rank ~15 of 210, and their function lists genuinely differ. But from the other players' chairs the two turns look identical: both spend an Action or a Reaction, both modify somebody else's roll, neither ever produces a number of their own. That similarity is not fixed by differentiating their keyword lists. It is fixed by giving each of them a verb they resolve on their own turn, and making those two verbs different from each other.

THE DIAGNOSTIC I JUDGE EVERY PROPOSAL BY. The property the two PCs are missing is not damage. It is a self-initiated, always-legal, always-resolves, visibly-scaled on-turn play. Damage is the cheapest way to buy that property, which is why it presents as the answer. It is not the only way, and for these two trees it is the wrong way — see the damage argument.

proposals.title: Give White a depth-0, 1-Action, self-resolving play that binds an ENEMY — the mortal-scale Edict
proposals.surface: data (data/leyline.json structure + data/authored/leyline-white.json) + pack rebuild; engine reuse only, no new primitive
proposals.change: Add ONE new depth-0 node to White's Accord specialty (White goes to 26 nodes — do NOT free a slot by deleting Hardy or Unity of Purpose, both are managed `connections` prerequisites and removing either is exactly the iron-rule-7 trap; the leyline guide's Principle 8 explicitly forbids imposing a uniform node count, so 26 is legal). Shape: prereq White 1+, no connections (White already carries 5 depth-0 entries where the other colours carry 4). 1 Action, 1 Investiture, test White vs. Cognitive defense against a creature in Attunement Range. On success the target is Bound until the start of your next turn under one behaviour you name from a fixed short list (move away from you / attack any creature other than you / take a Reaction); if it does the forbidden thing it takes [Tier][Die] spirit damage and the Bind ends. Add one depth-1 rider so the Bulwark half connects to it (an ally's hit on a Bound creature refreshes the Bind, or a Bound creature's violation grants the nearest ally temporary HP). CRITICAL IMPLEMENTATION NOTE: this is not new mechanics. deity/Order's Edict (data/authored/deity-order.json, depth 0, 1 Action, 1 Investiture, `(@tier)d(2 * @skills.blue.rank + 2) + @attr.int` spirit, Disoriented on violation) is the same machine, already wired and already shipping in Foundry — copy the event shape and change the tested colour to White. Keep White's version strictly mortal-scale: ONE Bind at a time (Order sustains up to Tier), until-your-next-turn (Order's persist for the scene), no Sealed/Witness layer.
proposals.resolves: Ledger #1 outright — White's 2-of-25 Action-costing count becomes 3-of-25 and, more importantly, the count of talents that produce an effect White resolves without another creature's cooperation goes from 1 (Retributive Guard, a Reaction) to 2 with one at level 1. It also closes an intent gap NOT in the ledger: INTENT-leyline-White.md promises Accord is 'authority made binding — terms, oaths, and disciplined will that COMPEL ENEMIES', and all eight Accord talents are ally-facing, negate-only, or ride the generic Influence action; no White talent proactively constrains an enemy on White's own turn. And it is the differentiation half of the 'same as their thing' problem: White becomes the marshal who dictates terms to an enemy, Blue stays the mage who stops the enemy moving.
proposals.cost: Deity/Order overlap is the real cost and needs naming: an Order character IS a White character (Blue 2+/White 2+), so a White+Order player would own two Edicts. Mitigated by the mortal/Radiant scale split — which is the stated design (leyline Principle 9: 'Radiant-equivalent power lives in the Deity Domain trees'), and White is currently the only colour that owns the mortal-scale version of NOTHING its deity trees do. Retest: pack rebuild + a bench pass on the new talent's event wiring; re-run validate.js's DAG/reachability (adding a root node is safe but prove it); White's Investiture load goes from 15 costers to 16 against a ~4 pool with zero regen, which is why proposal 3 pairs with this one.
proposals.confidence: HIGH that the gap is real and falsifiable (0 of 3 level-1 White picks are self-resolving; 0 of 8 Accord talents bind an enemy). MEDIUM-HIGH that this specific shape is the right remedy. What would change my mind: if Ben's intent is that White should never act on an enemy at all — but the path description says the opposite in its own words.

proposals.title: Bring Blue's lockdown down to Tier 1, and re-price Phantom Double so level-1 Blue has an affordable play
proposals.change: (a) Add a depth-0-or-1 Blue talent that is the Tier-1 rung of the movement-denial ladder Blue currently only reaches at L6: 1 Action, 1 Investiture, test Blue vs. Cognitive; on success the target is Slowed until the end of its next turn, and its movement rate becomes 0 instead if it was already Slowed. Ghostly Walls (Blue 3+, L6) then becomes the UPGRADE — re-scope it to scene-length or no-repeat-test so it is not dominated by the new entry, and Absolute Stillness keeps reading 'creatures you have reduced to 0 Speed', which the new talent can now produce from level 2. (b) Re-price Phantom Double from 2 Actions + 2 Investiture to 1 Action + 1 Investiture and give the duplicate health equal to [Die] rather than 1 — it is the only depth-0 talent in the leyline atlas costing 2 Investiture, i.e. half a level-1 pool, for an object that any single hit deletes. (c) Cheap adjacent fix: let Forewarned's granted Reaction pay for Intercept, so the tree's own two-talent combo does not cost two Investiture to express.
proposals.resolves: Ledger #1's Blue half and Blue's back-loading — Blue carries eight rank-3 gates, the most in the atlas, and its three signature effects (Counterspell, Ghostly Walls, Absolute Stillness) are all level 6, so the Blue player spends the entire tier-1 campaign with a kit that does not yet include the thing the tree is for. It gives Blue a repeatable, self-initiated, always-legal on-turn play whose result the whole table sees (the enemy did not get where it wanted to go), which is the exact property the diagnostic asks for, and does it without a point of damage.
proposals.cost: Blue becomes a genuinely strong tier-1 controller — movement denial is high-value in a 3-Action economy and this is a real power increase, not a rounding. Ghostly Walls must be re-scoped in the same change or it is strictly dominated by its own new entry rung. Retest the 0-Speed engine path end-to-end (Absolute Stillness and Redirect Momentum both read it) and the Slowed application. Phantom Double's re-price needs a bench check that the illusion object's health field takes a [Die] expression.
proposals.confidence: HIGH. The measurement is simple and reproducible: count Blue's L1-5 self-initiated plays (Phantom Double, Phantom Barricade, Read Intent at L4) against Red's or Black's. What would change my mind: if Ben wants Blue's tier-1 identity to be pure foreknowledge and the lockdown genuinely to be the level-6 reward — in which case (b) and (c) still stand on their own and (a) should become a foreknowledge play instead.

proposals.title: Give White and Blue one bonus-Investiture-regen talent each — the cheapest possible agency multiplier
proposals.surface: data + pack rebuild; the regen primitive already ships in nine talents
proposals.change: White and Blue are the only two leyline trees with ZERO bonus Investiture regeneration (Black has 2, Red has 2) while carrying 15 and 16 Investiture-costing talents respectively against a ~4 pool. At Tier 1 Draw Mana returns exactly 1 Investiture per Action, so a 1-Investiture-per-Action kit sustains at 50% uptime: one Action refuelling, one Action doing your thing. Give each tree one free Passive at depth 0-1, capped at once per round, on an on-identity trigger that is NOT self-funding. White: recover 1 Investiture when an ally within Attunement Range drops below half health, or when you Draw Mana while two or more allies are adjacent to you (formation-shaped, so it rewards the positioning the tree already wants). Blue: recover 1 Investiture when a creature you named with Forewarned takes the declared action, or when a creature within Attunement Range fails a test you imposed disadvantage on (prediction-shaped). Precedent and balance anchors already exist: leyline/Black's Sanguine Reservoir and Predator's Due, leyline/Red's two, and the free depth-0/1 Passives in Chaos (Void Sense), Death (Reaper's Harvest), Life (Prognosis), Knowledge (Accumulate) and Sovereignty (Expose).
proposals.resolves: Not a ledger item — a multiplier on every other proposal. It roughly doubles the number of rounds on which a White or Blue player gets to activate the thing they took a talent for, which is the literal content of 'I have nothing to do this round.' It also removes an unremarked asymmetry: the two trees with no damage are also the two trees with the worst economy.
proposals.cost: Raises both trees' sustained output by about one activation per two rounds, which compounds with proposals 1 and 2 — do NOT land all three without a bench pass measuring rounds-per-fight on a real encounter. The White trigger must not key on Draw Mana alone or it becomes an infinite loop (Draw Mana pays 1, regen pays 1). Retest the trigger's once-per-round guard specifically; every existing regen talent in the corpus has a limiter and Reaper's Harvest's lack of one is already noted as the outlier.
proposals.confidence: HIGH on the diagnosis (the 0-regen/15-coster and 0-regen/16-coster figures are directly countable in the dossiers). MEDIUM on the exact trigger wording — that is a design choice, not a determinable one.

proposals.title: Convert Blue's disadvantage block from the binary channel to the SUMMING numeric channel
proposals.surface: data (authored `events` on four talents) + a pinned regression case in tests/ per iron rule 4; NO new engine primitive
proposals.change: Blue imposes disadvantage on four talents (Pattern Recognition, Intercept, False Premise, Probability Cascade) plus a fifth adjacent effect. Per SYSTEM-PRIMER.md the engine folds all of these into one tri-state, so four talents do one talent's work and a second source on the same roll is worth literally zero. The engine ALREADY carries the alternative: `edha-next-test-mod` has a `formula` field applied by term concatenation, and item 49 made matching entries SUM. Re-author Blue's disadvantage riders as numeric penalties on that channel — -1d4 at Tier 1, -1d6 at Tier 2 — with a hard cap (recommend: total penalty dice may not exceed your Tier). Keep exactly ONE binary disadvantage in the tree so Blue can still hard-swing a single decisive roll.
proposals.resolves: The single biggest reason Blue produces nothing the table can see. A -1d6 on an enemy's attack is a number a player watches happen; a second disadvantage is invisible by construction. It also makes Blue's core verb unique in the corpus — no other tree imposes a numeric test penalty, so this differentiates Blue from every advantage/disadvantage granter in the game rather than adding a fifth copy of a shared effect.
proposals.cost: This is the least-proven path in the option set: `edha-next-test-mod`'s formula channel is used by exactly ONE adversary ability (Probability Net) and by zero talents, so Blue would be its first talent consumer. Uncapped additive numeric penalties are independently the ecosystem's largest identified balance risk — the cap is not optional. It also creates an asymmetry (Blue's penalties sum; every ally-facing advantage in the game stays binary) which is itself a design decision Ben has to make deliberately. Needs a pinned regression test and a full bench pass on all four talents plus their interaction with the existing binary sources.
proposals.confidence: MEDIUM. High confidence the binary collapse is real (the primer quotes the engine's own fold comment). Medium that summing is the right remedy rather than, say, cutting Blue's five disadvantage talents to two and spending the slots elsewhere. What would change my mind: a bench measurement showing the formula channel misbehaves when a binary disadvantage is also present on the same roll.

proposals.title: deity/Sovereignty: build the Decree. Deliver the promise rather than retract it
proposals.surface: data (all nine talents' targeting + data/authored/deity-sovereignty.json) and probably ONE engine addition — a zone that applies different riders by disposition
proposals.change: Convert Censure and Exalt from single-target actions into a placed DECREE: 1 Action, 1 Investiture, declare a Decree centred on a point in Attunement Range with radius [Size]; while it stands, enemies inside are Censured (damage die down one step) and allies inside are Exalted (up one step); sustain up to your Tier. The other seven talents keep their text almost verbatim but now read 'each creature affected by your Decree' instead of 'a creature' — so Sovereign's Favor's [Tier][Die] temp HP, Expose's Investiture refund and Reactive Strike grant, Edict of the Fallen's per-miss party temp HP and the capstone's reaction lock all multiply by the number of bodies inside. Reuse the zone machinery already shipped for deity/Fate's Ordained Ground and leyline/Green's difficult terrain; the new part is a zone whose rider differs by disposition, which Ordained Ground (ally-only) does not currently do.
proposals.resolves: Ledger #4 entirely, and it is the rare fix where delivering the promise IS the balance fix. It repairs (a) the documentation drift — the path description a player reads before choosing their god promises 'a declared law projected within a radius' and no talent creates a radius; (b) the perceptibility failure — one die step is +1.0 average damage and is worth exactly ZERO against the four flat-damage riders in the corpus, but one die step across three bodies is three die steps and reads as an event; (c) the two-repeated-clauses monotony, because the nine talents now differ by geometry rather than only by duration; (d) part of ledger #2, since Sovereignty acquires a genuine multi-target answer where it currently has none.
proposals.cost: The largest single change in this set — every one of nine talents' targeting and authored rules is touched, and the tree becomes materially stronger (a sustained zone that diminishes every enemy inside is a lot for 1 Action). The elevate half's headroom problem survives untouched: a rank-3 ally rolling d8 has only two rungs to the d12 cap, so Investiture of Authority (+1 scene) and the capstone (+2 scene) still cannot both pay out on the same ally. Full bench pass on the tree, plus a new zone type to test. Do not attempt this in the same pass as proposals 1-3.
proposals.confidence: HIGH that the Decree gap is real (grep the tree for radius/aura/zone/area: nothing; 'Decree' appears only inside one talent's name) and that geometry is the correct fix. MEDIUM on scope — if the zone rider-by-disposition turns out to need real engine work, proposal 10 is the fallback. What would change my mind: if the intent source is simply stale and Ben never wanted a zone, in which case only proposal 10(b) is owed.

proposals.title: The determinable batch — eight fixes that need no ruling and can ship this week
proposals.change: (a) leyline/White Interposing Shield reads `half [Die]` where its two siblings Devoted Conduit and Shield Wall read `half [Tier][Die]` — so White's COSTED Reaction mitigates ~2.0 at Tier 2 while its FREE Passives mitigate ~4.5. One-token fix. (b) data/leyline.json:840 Counterspell's cost reads '2 Focus; 1 Investiure' — a typo that silently removes it from every automated census and has already made two analyses report Blue's coster count wrong. (c) deity/Death Raise Dead (`connections` names Risen Servant, which the card never mentions, and omits Speak with the Fallen, which it does) and Necrotic Cascade (`connections` silently ANDs Death Ward onto the card's stated Consuming Decay) — iron rule 7's ungated third case, live on main, and the felt symptom is a player picking a talent and Foundry refusing with no reason on the card. (d) White's Mending Aura: the source prose owes the '1 Investiture' the authored text already charges. (e) deity/Power Kneel and Absolute Authority both key off Frightened, which NO talent in the corpus produces — either strike the word or add a producer. (f) deity/Chaos Unravel Everything is the only one of ten deity capstones with no once-per-scene limiter. (g) leyline/White Shared Burden is dated L6 because the tooling applied the SKILL rank cap to `Strength 3+`, which is an ATTRIBUTE gate (points at levels 3/6/9) — re-date it. (h) Unify the two temporary-HP writers: module-src/scripts/engine/28-temporary-hp.js contradicts itself seven lines apart ('a larger grant replaces a smaller one' vs 'a new grant OVERWRITES the old, even if smaller') and 51-green-restoration.js:93 implements keep-the-higher; the authored description on Sovereignty's Sovereign's Favor asserts keep-the-higher too, so two of three sources agree and that is the recommended default.
proposals.resolves: Ledger items 5, 7, 9, 15, 16, 18 and 20. (a) and (c) are the two the players will actually feel — a Reaction that stops being underwhelming, and a talent pick that stops being refused for no printed reason.
proposals.cost: Near zero. (h) is the only one with any risk and it invalidates every temp-HP-summed-over-rounds figure produced in this review until it lands, so do it before any further temp-HP arithmetic. (c) touches `connections`, so re-run validate.js's DAG and reachability sweeps even though the edit is a repair.
proposals.confidence: VERY HIGH — every item is checkable against a named file and line.

proposals.title: Unclog White's Reaction slot: three talents fire on one trigger and compete for one slot per round
proposals.surface: data + pack rebuild; graph surgery, so validate.js must be re-run
proposals.change: White holds seven Reactions against a hard cap of one per round, and three of them — Interposing Shield ('an ally within 10 feet takes damage'), Retributive Guard ('an ally adjacent to you takes damage from an enemy') and Shared Burden ('an ally adjacent to you takes damage') — fire on the same event. Two options, pick one: (i) merge those three into a single Reaction with an upgrade ladder purchased by later talents (reduce the damage → punish the attacker → take it in their place), freeing two slots to spend on the Accord/on-turn side from proposal 1; or (ii) leave the talents alone and add one White talent granting a SECOND Reaction usable only for Bulwark talents — the precedent is heroic/Envoy's Foresight, which grants an unconditional extra Reaction, so an effect-limited version is comfortably inside existing power.
proposals.resolves: The second half of ledger #1. White's remaining 23 non-Action slots are 10 Passives, 6 Specials and 7 Reactions; the Passives are always on and fine, but the Reactions cannibalise each other and a player who has bought three of them uses one. Option (ii) is strictly the safer of the two.
proposals.cost: Option (i) is graph surgery in a tree with live `connections` edges — Shield Wall connects to Shared Burden AND Hardy, and Interposing Shield connects to Pillar of Order and Guardian Stance. Merging nodes severs managed prerequisites, which is precisely the iron-rule-7 territory this review already found two live violations in. Option (ii) costs one node and no edges. Retest: bench the extra-Reaction grant against the engine's per-round Reaction accounting.
proposals.confidence: MEDIUM-HIGH on the diagnosis (the three trigger texts are quotable and identical in substance). MEDIUM on the remedy — I would take option (ii) and only revisit (i) if the bench shows the slot is still the binding constraint.

proposals.title: Give each leyline colour one multi-enemy answer reachable before level 6
proposals.surface: data + pack rebuild across up to five trees
proposals.change: Fourteen of twenty-one trees can never damage two enemies with one play at any level; before level 6, exactly TWO trees have a repeatable unconditional multi-enemy play (deity/Destruction's Set Charge at L1, leyline/Red's Flame Surge at L2). The party this review was commissioned about holds White and Blue — both zero — and heroic paths, five of six of which are zero and the sixth of which (Warrior's Meteoric Leap) is level 6, unarmed and behind Athletics 3+. Give each leyline colour one Tier-1-reachable talent that affects more than one enemy in its own idiom rather than porting Red's fireball everywhere: White a formation effect that penalises enemies adjacent to two or more of your allies (which rewards the positioning White already wants); Blue an illusion that forces every enemy within [Size] to test or lose track of a chosen target; Green already owns zones. Separately, rebuild leyline/Black's Spoils of Isolation, which is an INVERTED area attack — it hits 'each Weakened character in Attunement Range', and Black's only two Weakened sources both require the target to have no ally within 5 feet, so Black's area damage scales with the enemies being SPREAD OUT and does nothing against a clump.
proposals.resolves: Ledger #2, and the party-level statement none of the thirteen analyses made: if the other PCs hold heroic paths, this party has no answer to four enemies in any of its available trees, and the GM cannot put a group on the table without the fight becoming a queue.
proposals.cost: Broad — up to five trees touched, and it is the proposal most likely to have knock-on balance effects, because area damage is the single most swingy category in an encounter. It also cannot be settled inside the review's scope fence: whether the right budget is 'most trees can hit a group' or 'groups are one specialist's job' depends on whether minion packs are the encounter norm, which lives in the adversary statblocks that are explicitly out of scope. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a count of enemies-per-encounter across the built adversary set and the session-1 encounter roster.
proposals.confidence: MEDIUM. The census itself is solid and reproducible; the correct target-count budget is not determinable from the 365 talents.

proposals.title: THE EXPLICIT DAMAGE OPTION for White — costed, and ranked here deliberately
proposals.change: If the designer wants a damage concession, the on-identity shape for White is NOT a nuke and NOT an area: promote the [Tier][Die] spirit line that already exists on Retributive Guard from a Reaction into a repeatable Special that rides White's OWN Strike while an ally is adjacent — 'the line strikes together'. Spirit is already White's declared damage type (its one damage formula is `(@tier)d(2 * @skills.white.rank + 2)` type=spirit), so this adds no new vocabulary, keeps the adjacency condition that is White's whole identity, and costs a Special rather than an Action so it does not compete with the agency fix in proposal 1. Explicitly do NOT give White a ranged bolt or an area — those are Red and Black, and White taking them is the fastest way to turn a distinct tree into a worse copy of two others.
proposals.resolves: The surface complaint the review was commissioned about ('two characters in paths with NO damage talents'), and nothing else.
proposals.cost: It does not fix the actual defect. White's problem is 2 Action-costing talents in 25, not 1 damage talent in 25 — a Special that rides a Strike adds zero Action-costing slots and leaves 22 contingent ones untouched. It erodes the one axis on which White is the game's reference implementation (protection), moves White into Red and Black's function space at a moment when Black<->Red at 0.920 is already the corpus's most similar pair, and does nothing at all for 'my thing is the same as their thing' — a small spirit-damage rider is the most generic effect in the game. It is also the most reversible proposal here, which is its one virtue: if proposals 1-3 land and the bench still reports dead rounds, this is cheap to add afterwards.
proposals.confidence: HIGH that this is the wrong FIRST move and a defensible LATER one. What would change my mind: a bench pass after proposals 1-3 in which the White player still reports that their turns do not register at the table — that would mean the missing property is legibility of outcome, and in this system legibility means a number.

proposals.title: Sovereignty fallback if proposal 5 is too large — two edits instead of nine
proposals.surface: data (data/path-descriptions.json for (b); leyline-scale authored edits for (a))
proposals.change: (a) Make the payload perceptible without building the zone: change Exalt and Censure from 'one die step' alone to 'one die step AND +/-[Tier] to damage rolls'. The die step is +1.0 average per die and is worth exactly ZERO against the four flat-damage riders in the corpus (Momentum of Victory, Cheap Shot, Pack Share, Vital Diagnosis), so today a Sovereignty player can spend an Action and an Investiture on an ally and produce a mathematically null result. (b) REGARDLESS of whether (a) or proposal 5 happens, correct data/path-descriptions.json so the promised signature resource matches the nine shipped talents. The current text promises in bold 'a declared law projected within a radius: allies inside are elevated, enemies inside are diminished' and every one of the nine targets a single creature. A player reads that text when choosing which god their character serves — it is the first thing the tree tells them and it is not true.
proposals.resolves: Ledger #4's documentation half and its perceptibility half. Leaves the target-count and two-clause-redundancy halves open.
proposals.cost: (a) risks stacking with deity/Knowledge's Insight multiplier and deity/Life's Vital Diagnosis rider on the same marked ally — check that interaction before shipping. (b) has no mechanical cost at all and is the one item in this proposal I would ship unconditionally: either build the Decree or stop promising it.
proposals.confidence: HIGH on (b) — it is a two-source contradiction anyone can verify in thirty seconds. MEDIUM on (a), which is a design judgment about how big a Sovereignty Action should feel.

singleFirstChange:
Proposal 1: give leyline/White one depth-0, 1-Action, 1-Investiture, self-resolving talent that binds an ENEMY under a declared prohibition and punishes violation with [Tier][Die] spirit damage — built by copying deity/Order's already-shipping Edict event shape and swapping the tested colour to White, kept mortal-scale (one Bind, expires at your next turn, no Sealed layer).

Why this one above everything else, including the cheaper fixes: session one has not been played, and at level 1 the White player picks from three talents of which ZERO produce an effect they resolve themselves. Every other proposal in this set makes an existing play land more often, land harder, or land on more targets. This is the only one that gives the White player something to do on the first turn of the first fight. It is also the cheapest kind of new content in the repo — a proven event shape, no new engine primitive, no graph surgery, and no other tree gets weaker.
argumentOnBlueWhiteDamage:
POSITION: NO to damage for both, as the fix. YES to exactly one narrow damage concession for White, later, if the agency fixes fail — and NO to damage for Blue under any reading.

THE ARGUMENT. The designer's framing was 'two characters in paths with NO damage talents', and that is a true and easily-measured fact that is nonetheless not the defect. Damage is doing duty in that sentence as a proxy for four properties at once: an effect that is self-initiated, always legal, always resolves, and produces a visible number. Those four properties are what the two players are missing, and damage is simply the cheapest single purchase of all four. Buy the properties directly and the trees stay distinct; buy the damage and you get the properties plus a fifth thing nobody wants, which is White and Blue drifting toward Red and Black.

The measurement that decides it. White has ONE damage talent (Retributive Guard). Giving it a second would take White from 1/25 to 2/25 and would leave the actual number — 2 of 25 talents you can spend an Action on, the lowest in all 21 trees, against deity trees at 5-8 of 9 — completely unmoved, because a damage rider is a Special or a Reaction and adds no Action-costing slot. If instead you accept that White's problem is 2/25, then the fix is by definition a talent White ACTIVATES, and once you are writing an activated White talent the question 'should it deal damage or should it bind an enemy' answers itself from the path description: 'binding enemies to terms they cannot break' is White's own stated Accord specialty and no White talent does it.

Blue is a stronger no. Blue's win condition is that the enemy does not get to act — Counterspell, Ghostly Walls, Absolute Stillness, the disadvantage block. Damage works against that identity rather than with it: a Blue mage who kills an enemy has produced the same board state as a Blue mage who locked it, at a job Red and Black do 2-6x better per Action, using an Investiture pool Blue cannot refill. Blue's missing property is legibility, not lethality, and proposals 2 and 4 buy legibility directly — an enemy that visibly does not reach the fighter, and a -1d6 the whole table watches land — without a point of damage and without a fifth copy of an effect five other trees already have.

THE ONE CONCESSION I WOULD ACCEPT, and its precondition. If proposals 1, 2 and 3 land and a bench pass STILL shows the White player reporting turns that do not register at the table, then the missing property was legibility of outcome, and in this system legibility means a number. At that point give White — not Blue — a Special that rides White's own Strike for [Tier][Die] spirit while an ally is adjacent (proposal 9). Spirit is already White's only damage type, adjacency is already White's whole identity, and it costs no Action. Never a ranged bolt, never an area: those belong to Red and Black, and the corpus's most similar pair is already Black<->Red at 0.920.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE MY MIND, stated so it can be tested rather than argued. Run the bench with proposals 1-3 landed and count, per fight, per player: (i) Actions the White/Blue player spent on a talent versus on Draw Mana, Move or an unsupported Strike; (ii) rounds in which they activated nothing; (iii) whether another player at the table could name what they did. If (ii) is still high, agency was not the constraint and I am wrong about the diagnosis. If (ii) drops but (iii) stays low, the constraint is legibility and the damage concession is correct. Both are cheap to measure and neither is answerable from the talent data alone.
argumentOnSovereignty:
Sovereignty is the one tree in this review where I would DELIVER the promise rather than retract it, because the promise is also the balance fix.

The felt experience, which is why it belongs in a player-experience pass even though no PC is in it. A player choosing which god their character serves reads a bolded line promising 'a declared law projected within a radius: allies inside are elevated, enemies inside are diminished.' They then get nine talents, every one of which targets a single creature, and 'Decree' appears nowhere except inside the name 'Decree of Ruin'. Their first turn is: one Action, one Investiture, and their friend's damage die goes from d6 to d8 — an average of +1.0, and exactly zero against the four flat-damage riders in the corpus. That is below the threshold at which a human at a table perceives that anything happened, and it is the whole tree: eight of nine talents are the same two clauses ('increases by one step, maximum d12' / 'decreases by one step, minimum d4') differing only in duration.

Why the radius fixes four things at once. Give Censure and Exalt a Decree footprint and: the documentation drift closes; the payload becomes perceptible because one die step across three bodies is three die steps; the two-clause monotony becomes a geometry problem instead of a duration problem; and Sovereignty acquires the multi-target answer that fourteen of twenty-one trees lack. No other proposal in this set repairs four ledger symptoms with one structural change.

The honest counterweight. Sovereignty is NOT empty, and the 'damage_direct 0, nine axes at zero' framing is partly an artefact of a rubric with no cell for an amplifier that never swings — deity/Knowledge does the identical job and scores 5/5 because it also holds a sword. Expose is a free level-2 Passive that generates Investiture uncapped and converts every enemy miss into an ally's Reactive Strike; Sovereign's Favor grants [Tier][Die] temp HP on every Exalt, unmediated by the die ladder; Edict of the Fallen is a scene-long two-step debuff plus party temp HP. And White 3+ is NOT the pure toll booth it was reported as — `data/authored/deity-sovereignty.json` sizes Sovereign's Favor's temp HP on `(@tier)d(2 * @skills.white.rank + 2)`, so the gate does buy something. It just buys it invisibly, because every Sovereignty card prints '[Tier][Die]' and names no colour, so a player choosing between a third rank of Black and a third of White is choosing blind. Printing the colour on the card is a one-word fix and should happen regardless of everything else.

MINIMUM OWED, whatever else is decided: correct `data/path-descriptions.json`. Either build the Decree or stop promising it — a player should not meet the tree's central lie before they have rolled a die.
